_comment: Tier-2 for skfem hydraulic_resistance#4, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: computing the flow rate with the volumetric Basis instead of FacetBasis 'double-counts interior edges and produces a Q that's ~2x too large', with R_fe half of R_exact. Ran: the shipped channel discretisation at four channel lengths L = 1, 2, 3, 5, computing the outlet flux both ways and also summing basis.dx and facet.dx. Printed: THE FACTOR IS NOT 2 AND THE MECHANISM IS NOT DOUBLE-COUNTING. The volumetric form computes an AREA integral, which for this flow equals Q times the channel length, so the wrong/right ratio tracks L exactly: 1.0130, 2.0393, 3.0676, 5.1227 at L = 1, 2, 3, 5. It reads as '2x' only because the template's default length is 2. At L = 1 the mistake is nearly invisible -- within 1.3% -- so a gate calibrated on '2x' passes it, and the error grows without bound as the channel lengthens. 'R_fe is half of R_exact' inherits the same defect: it is R divided by the LENGTH. Nothing warns about the wrong integral; the only warning skfem emits is a style deprecation on the template's own interpolate(u).value[0] idiom, which fires identically for both integrals and so carries no information. The dimensional guard that always works: sum(basis.dx) is the domain area and sum(facet.dx) is the outlet length.
